This process, called histopathological characterization, involves accurately identifying specific tissue abnormalities and their severity levels through a process called scoring. With the constant evolution of imaging technologies and machine learning algorithms, there is growing interest in substituting expert human judgment with automated analysis methods. In this context, we present a publicly accessible dataset of annotated histopathological images of colorectal polyps, which can serve as a benchmark for evaluating the performance of deep learning algorithms in both classification and scoring tasks.

A novel numerical approach has been introduced for solving time-harmonic diffusion problems characterized by smoothly varying conductivity and scattering coefficients. This method employs an experimentally verified mathematical principle and leverages the slowness of variation to justify finely tuned numerical mesh refinement. A crucial aspect of this approach is the ability to incorporate implicit and explicit boundary conditions. Computational experiments demonstrate that this technique yields accurate and reliable results, outperforming existing methods by a significant order of magnitude in terms of computational time for difficult cases.

We examined the water content in small particles from the Chelyabinsk and Benenitra meteorites, which originated from the inner solar system based on their Benitoite-bearing and absence of Benitoite respectively. By comparing their water levels to models of solar system material, we found a higher water content in Chelyabinsk than Benenitra, with an average of 1.2-1.5 times more water in Chelyabinsk. This difference can be attributed to a 2-3 times greater abundance of hydrous silicate minerals in Chelyabinsk, which is consistent with previous analyses of how the inner solar system was formed. The higher water content in Chelyabinsk suggests that many small bodies in the inner solar system were affected by a dry solar wind during its early active phase of massive flares and coronal mass ejections. The water content in these inner solar system planetesimals most likely originated from a source rich in carbon monoxide and organic compounds, which were then combined with hydrogen to form water molecules during the process of accretion.

Building on the low-lying excitation spectrum of the XXZ chain, higher-spin XXZ chain analogues are introduced, based on representations of the affine quantum group $U_q(\hat{e(2))}$, with $q$ not necessarily equal to one. These new models possess an exact, self-dual point where their spin-1/2 and spin-j sectors relate to each other through the duality rotation, and further, this self-dual point is reached when the boundary reflections of lattice excitations are symmetric. At this self-dual point, the structure factors of these higher-spin XXZ chains are shown to match those of the integrable XXZ chain, and thus, these structure factors are herself-dual, in that they only depend on the differences of the high-spin XXZ chain's excitation eigenvalues, and not its individual values.

Language barriers persist as primary obstacles in disaster response, healthcare, and other critical situations, largely due to the limitations and cost-prohibitive nature of human translation. Machine translation has made significant progress in recent years but still falls short in several areas, notably in low-resource and high-quality settings. One such setting is one-to-many language translation from an unknown source language. This paper introduces a novel approach to achieve zero-shot translation, a feat previously only accomplished by concurrently sharing source and target language information with the model. By employing a rotation equivariant layer and a novel memory-augmented attention mechanism within a neural machine translation framework, we have successfully achieved this advancement. Our experiments across five zero-shot translation scenarios and two memory-augmented settings demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, with results outperforming the baseline system by a substantial 23%.

We extend the Mie series to a multipolar form, applicable for arbitrary wave lengths. This new approach uses vector spherical harmonics and Radon transform-based multipolar coefficients. Our method accurately describe the electric and magnetic fields around a sphere, even when it's highly illuminated or has complex, irregular surface features. By simulating electromagnetic field interactions with a small particle, our method can also be used to analyze light scattering, optical force, and radiation pressure. By further integrating our approach with numerical tools, we can compute quantities like the optical force and force correlations for arbitrary configurations.

This study introduces an element, denoted as $\tilde{e}_\lambda$, which serves as a quantum equivalent to the immanant $\chi_\lambda$ for structured Schur functions, including those from the double Young-Capelli basis and certain altered symmetric functions. It was previously established that the quantum immanants $\tilde{e}_\lambda$ possess a combinatorial interpretation mirroring that of their classical counterparts, $\chi_\lambda$, except in cases where $\lambda$ consists of a single row. In such instances, $\tilde{e}_\lambda$ alters the original interpretation, replacing row standardization with a more complex tableaux modeling standardization process. As a result, $\tilde{e}_\lambda$ can be viewed as a sum of elements from both the double Young-Capelli basis and altered symmetric functions, ultimately providing a representation of these elements within the quantum group algebra. It is also demonstrated that the elementary components of these structured Schur functions, when represented in the Fock space, equivalently use Ustimenkow's theorem to determine their values, or a direct computation method.

We've developed an easy-to-understand "scoto-seesaw" framework for neutrino oscillation, which incorporates a minimal "dark sector" consisting of neutrinos and a dark scalar. Within this framework, we've explored the "dark R-parity" violation (DRPV) mechanism, which enables the direct coupling of the dark scalar to standard model particles while suppressing the same coupling for neutrinos. As a result, neutrinos remain stable, meeting the requirements for warm dark matter. Furthermore, we've determined that the DRPV mechanism can successfully generate the appropriate abundance of dark matter. In addition, we've investigated the production of the dark scalar at the Large Hadron Collider and found its detection to be within its sensitivity range. Additionally, we've analyzed the stability of the vacuum in the standard model with an additional neutrino dimensionless parameter and found it to be robust against the effects of neutrino violation up to an extremely high threshold.

We employ a combination of ab initio and model Hamiltonian techniques to
examine the electronic structure of late 3d, 4d, and 5d transition metal
oxides, with particular attention on how $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbital states blend
as we move from 3d to 5d systems. These calculations are grounded in
featureless LDA$+$U band structures and are contrasted with the results of
harmonically perturbed models, showing that the splitting of the $e_g$
orbitals diminishes with increasing d-fertility, while the $t_{2g}$ doublet
remains largely intact. Additionally, in 4d and 5d compounds, with strong
correlation, the $e_g$ splitting becomes negative, as observed in some
experimentally measured spectra. These findings are attributed to the
increasing interference of $e_g$ and $t_{2g}$ molecular orbitals with further
extension of the d shell. Consequently, this analysis cautions against
unreserved use of 3d transition metal physics intuition in the study of 4d
and 5d compounds and suggests that the electronic structure may exhibit a
more subtle d-fertility-dependent blend.

This study examines how relative quantum homology changes under a certain type of symplectic transformation called rational transformations. These transformations involve changing the symplectic form and shifting the coordinate on a specific symplectic manifold while keeping the underlying topological structure constant. We demonstrate that the relative quantum homology's symmetry properties are conserved under rational transformations, and further derive a precise formula to calculate its invariant.

The constantly evolving nature of the COVID-19 pandemic necessitates rapid, low-cost, and widely accessible screening methods for COVID-19 and other respiratory conditions. Using X-ray images for this purpose is an appealing option due to their widespread use and low cost. However, access to X-ray machines is limited in some areas, creating inequality in disease detection rates. To overcome this obstacle, we explore the potential for transforming any bright image into a realistic chest X-ray. Successfully achieving this could enable the use of existing datasets and models for disease prediction on modified images, thus making them applicable to real-world imaging scenarios.

Reducing high-dimensional data into lower-dimensional space has long been a common statistical approach used to visualize and simplify complex data sets for more in-depth analysis. A vast array of techniques is available for this dimension reduction, including Multidimensional Scaling, t-Distributed Neighborhood Mapping, and Variational Autoencoders. Despite the abundance of methods, none are universally considered best, as each data set requires a different technique to accurately preserve the initial data's nuances. Among the many available tools for nonlinear dimension reduction are ViDaExpert and the t-SNE package by Ljubica, both of which are explored in this study. ViDaExpert is a cutting-edge tool that offers a comprehensive and user-friendly interface for a variety of nonlinear dimension reduction techniques, including both classic and cutting-edge methods like VAE and Graph Neural Networks. Additionally, ViDaExpert enables users to easily incorporate prior knowledge into the data analysis process and offers several visualisation options to facilitate in-depth data examination and discovery.

This study proposes a rapid, straightforward method for calculating potential fields in flat areas, specifically in two-dimensional spaces. The method excels in simplicity, reducing the computational burden to a mere fraction of more complex techniques. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach by adapting it to a challenging scenario, namely when there are an infinite number of particles with the same mass distribution. The simplified method also lends itself easily to visualisation, as shown in the appended diagram.
